concept: Uninterruptible Us+ rank processes in the Thunderbolt RDMA driver
summary: `Us+` ranks drift into the state gradually after their launcher dies, so a sweep at the next restart can still kill the newest orphans

facts.text: `Us+` ranks drift into the state gradually after their launcher dies, so a sweep at the next restart can still kill the newest orphans
Orphaned ranks and their parent `sshd` both hang, so the orphan's ppid is the stuck `sshd`, not 1
`launchd` KeepAlive restarts re-ran `mlx.launch` within seconds and accumulated peer orphans each cycle
The fix kills all processes matching the model's `--tmpdir` pattern with `kill -9` before launching, with no ppid filter
A PID-file lock released just before `exec` prevents a manual run and a launchd restart from killing each other's ranks, since an EXIT trap does not fire after `exec`
Killed `mlx_lm.share` ranks left temp directories of 817 GB and 868 GB on two nodes; kill processes before deleting them
Ranks already in `Us+` survive `kill -9` and only a node reboot clears them
